description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, while fixing the inlet-enthalpy BC (op-2qsf). NOT fixed -- this is a discretisation-scheme question, deliberately left alone rather than half-fixed.

SYMPTOM. The energy equation's explicit convection term is fvc::div(&self.phi, &self.he), and fvc::div interpolates the convected scalar with fvc::interpolate, i.e. LINEAR (central) interpolation. The energy equation is advection-dominated (cell Peclet >> 1 for a gas), so an advancing thermal front carries dispersive over/undershoots.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, 0.5 m/s, dt 2e-4 s, uniform seed with a step inlet BC):
  seed 300 K, inlet BC 500 K: at 3000 steps the inlet cell reads 556.52 kJ/kg against a 520.45 kJ/kg BC -- 117 % of the imposed step, i.e. a 36 kJ/kg overshoot; at 10000 steps interior cells reach 571 K, above both the 500 K inlet and the 300 K seed.
  seed 500 K, inlet BC 300 K: at 3000 steps the inlet cell reads 296.13 kJ/kg against a 311.20 kJ/kg BC; at 10000 steps a cell reaches 274.45 K, ~25 K below anything imposed.
Magnitude is ~10-15 % of the imposed step on this 8-cell mesh -- textbook central-difference dispersion, not an instability (the fields stay finite and bounded over 10000 steps, damped by the alpha_h laplacian).

WHAT A FIX WOULD BE. OpenFOAM's rhoPimpleFoam does not use plain linear for div(phi,h) -- upwind or a limited scheme (limitedLinear / vanLeer) is the norm. The fvc::muscl / fvc::reconstruct_pos_neg machinery for a limited face reconstruction already exists in openfoam_source and is used by the HybridAllMach KNP path, so the pieces are there.

WHY NOT DONE HERE. (a) it is a scheme change, not a BC fix; (b) fvc::div is shared vendored code used by every solver path and by the sibling tampines-steam-tables copy, so changing it moves numbers across both crates; (c) any change to it must be justified against the crate's existing V&V numbers rather than slipped in. Document, measure, then decide.

Recorded in the doc comment of lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_enthalpy_bc_heats_uniform_field_without_reapplying_each_step so a reader meets the caveat where they meet the test.
title: OPCPFluidArray energy equation: div(phi,h) is pure central differencing -- dispersive over/undershoot at an advected thermal front

description:
get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_subcooled_liquid_ph (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs) returns the bubble-point sonic-kink flux rho_f*c_2phi whenever the two-phase quality at the energy-balance maximum is < 0.03 and the v_b/c_2phi ratio has not exceeded DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO = 5.0. The file's own comment block flags this as the 'overlap zone' and says no local discriminator separates it, for want of experimental data.

Marviken test 24 is that experimental data, and it lands squarely in the overlap zone. Measured 2026-08-11 (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/tests/marviken_tests.rs, bead op-21g.16):

- dispatcher vs Marviken test 24 (33 K subcooling, 40 points, NUREG/CR-2671 Fig 8:24): mean deviation -48.5 %, worst -70.2 %, 31 of 40 points outside the justified +/-25 % experimental band. The returned flux is nearly pressure-independent (16.85-16.95 Mg/m2 s) while the measurement rises 16.7 -> 56.6 Mg/m2 s.
- the BARE HEM maximum-mass-flux criterion (max over p of rho(p,s0)*sqrt(2(h0-h(p,s0))), built from the crate's public (p,s) flashes with no branch heuristics) on the identical case: mean deviation 9.0 %, signed bias -1.8 %, i.e. inside the band and essentially unbiased.
- same comparison on Marviken test 23 (3 K subcooling): dispatcher 12.6 %, bare criterion 10.1 %.

So the deficit is branch selection, not HEM physics. This is the SECOND time an apparent HEM limitation in this crate turned out to be a choke-finder branch problem (the first was the near-bubble-point artifact fixed in v0.2.1 — and that fix is what introduces this one).

Deliberately NOT fixed inside op-21g.16: retuning DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO against the very dataset used to validate would be fitting the model to its own validation case, and the current threshold is what protects the Zaloudek near-saturation curves (v_b/c_2phi <= 3.30 across all of them).

Work: find a discriminator that routes deeply-subcooled-but-below-5.0 states to the energy-balance maximum without disturbing any Zaloudek curve. Marviken 23/24 and the Moody deep-subcooled points now provide the constraint from the Bernoulli side; Zaloudek constrains the sonic side. Any change must keep all Zaloudek in-dome/subcooled/superheated tests green AND move marviken_tests::validate_against_marviken_test_24 from its characterisation envelope to the +/-25 % validation band — that test's assertions are written so it FAILS loudly if the deficit changes, and its doc comment plus the crate README/CLAUDE.md must be rewritten from 'characterisation' to 'validation' in the same change.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
CORRECTION TO COMMIT e11989a7's MESSAGE, recorded 2026-08-11.

That commit says 'test 24 bare-HEM: mean|dev| = 9.0%' and frames it as 'HEM tracks the full-scale Marviken data to about 9% on average'. **That framing is misleading and this note is the correction of record**, since the commit is already pushed and cannot be cleanly amended.

THE ACTUAL RESULT, from the fleet's final report:
- Test 23 (3 K subcooling): VALIDATED. Mean |dev| 12.6%, inside a measured +/-25%-per-point digitisation budget.
- Test 24 (33 K subcooling): **NOT validated through the production dispatcher — a -48.5% SYSTEMATIC deficit.**
- The 9.0% (test 24) and 10.1% (test 23) figures are from the **bare HEM maximum-flux criterion**, NOT the production path.

So the commit quoted a bare-criterion number as if it characterised the model's production behaviour, and omitted that the dispatcher is nearly 50% low on test 24.

WHY THAT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS GOOD NEWS: the gap between the bare criterion (9.0%) and the dispatcher (-48.5%) is the evidence that this is a SOLVER BRANCH-SELECTION DEFECT, not a limitation of HEM physics. HEM itself reproduces test 24 to 9%; the dispatcher is picking the wrong branch. That is this bead, it is P1, and it is fixable — unlike a physics limitation, which would not be.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CROSS-FIDELITY COMPARISON: the sibling fleet building drift-flux and two-fluid Marviken cases was released against a stated HEM reference. They must compare against the BARE-CRITERION numbers (9.0% / 10.1%) as the honest HEM baseline, NOT the dispatcher's -48.5%, which reflects this defect rather than the equilibrium assumption. Comparing a higher-fidelity model against a broken branch selection would flatter it for the wrong reason.

Also corrected in the same report: test 23's subcooling is 3 K, not 33 K, against NUREG/CR-2671.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
Diagnostic probe written 2026-08-11 and DELIBERATELY REVERTED, not committed — it was marked "TEMPORARY DIAGNOSTIC PROBE — REMOVE BEFORE COMMIT" in the source and was still in the working tree when the session died at ~12:52. Recording it here so the next person can re-create it in one paste instead of re-deriving it.

Location: get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_subcooled_liquid_ph, in
crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs,
inserted immediately after `subcooling_ratio` is computed and before the `if subcooling_ratio > DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO` branch. It required hoisting `let x_at_energy = two_phase_quality(p_energy, s0);` above that branch (it currently lives below it).

What it printed, one eprintln! per call, prefixed PROBE:
  branch       — which of the three arms is taken: "deep_escape" (subcooling_ratio > DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO), "sonic_kink" (x_at_energy < 0.03), or "energy"
  p0_MPa, h0_kJkg, T0_K   — the stagnation state
  dTsub_K      — sat_temp_4(p0) - T0, i.e. actual stagnation subcooling (NaN above p_crit)
  subratio     — the subcooling_ratio the deep-escape test uses
  x_at_energy  — the quality at the energy-maximum choke, i.e. the sonic-kink discriminator
  p_bub_MPa, p_energy_MPa, pe_over_pb   — the two candidate choke pressures and their ratio
  g_energy, g_sonic, ratio_ge_gs        — the two candidate mass fluxes and their ratio
  interior     — g_two_phase >= g_bubble, i.e. whether the energy max is a genuine interior stationary point or just the bubble endpoint
  g_two_phase, g_bubble

Purpose: the bead's thesis is that the Marviken test-24 points land in the "overlap zone" where subcooling_ratio never reaches DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO = 5.0 while x_at_energy < 0.03, so the solver takes the bubble-point sonic-kink branch (rho_f * c_2phi) when it should not. The probe is what turns that from an inference into per-point evidence: run the Marviken gate with it in place and read the branch / subratio / x_at_energy columns for the 40 test-24 points.

Reminder from the sibling bead op-21g.16: do NOT retune DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO or the 0.03 quality threshold against the Marviken data — that is fitting the model to its own validation set. The discriminator needs an independent basis.

title: tampines-steam-tables: HEM subcooled choke takes the wrong branch — Marviken test 24 resolves the DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO overlap zone

description: GitHub issue #30 comment: 'I also want to be able to drag corners of the box for the digitiser ui to adjust the min and max x and y'. op-zfnh's persistent box already lets each of the 4 lines be dragged independently; this adds a corner hit-test (x-line + y-line intersection) so one drag moves both at once. Implemented in this pass: crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/mod.rs's image_panel -- ref_dragging_corner field, hit_ref_corner test, corner-handle overlay circles.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented in the same pass as filing. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/mod.rs:
- New `ref_dragging_corner: Option<(usize, usize)>` field (indices into `ref_px`: an x-index in {0,1} paired with a y-index in {2,3}).
- `hit_ref_corner` hit-tests the 4 corner points (intersection of an x-line and a y-line) with a slightly larger tolerance than a bare line, checked BEFORE the existing `hit_ref_line` so a corner grab takes priority over an edge grab at the same point.
- Dragging a corner sets both `ref_px[xi]` and `ref_px[yi]` together in one gesture.
- Small handle circles drawn at all 4 corners (highlighted yellow + enlarged while being dragged) for discoverability.
`cargo check -p kovan --all-targets` clean. Not committed yet.

title: kovan-gui: digitiser -- drag corners of the reference box (not just edges)
